demos.title: Are clinical decision support alerts helping? | evrai demo
demos.card_blurb: Benchmark results next to live clinician feedback: aggregate only, with small cells suppressed.
demos.description: Narrated demo: an administrator view that pairs published benchmark results with live clinician feedback on decision-support alerts. It shows aggregate figures only, suppresses small cells, and gives admins control of each agent's LLM transport.
demos.intro: Administrators need to know whether decision-support alerts earn their place in a clinician's day. This walkthrough shows the Effectiveness page. It pairs published benchmark results with live accept, dismiss and review feedback, reports acceptance with a confidence interval and the median time to review, and suppresses any cell too small to share. It then shows the admin-only runtime setting that picks realtime or batch LLM transport for each agent. A safety gate still keeps live PHI on realtime.
points: Benchmark precision, recall and cost per case, each with a confidence interval
Every alert counted in exactly one outcome cell, including ones resolved in the EHR
Small-cell suppression: counts under 11 are masked and rates are withheld
Admin-only realtime or batch transport, with the safety gate's reason shown on the page

chapters.save: Saving and the PHI safety gate

demos.disclosure: This recording runs on a local demo stack. The benchmark results are aggregate figures from a public, de-identified research dataset (the MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo); all other data, including every patient, user, facility and alert count, is synthetic. It is not a live customer deployment and shows no protected health information. The narration is a synthetic, computer-generated voice.

demos.title: Role, credential and PHI access governance | evrai demo
demos.card_blurb: Least-privilege roles, a value-free credential inventory, and a searchable PHI access log.
demos.description: Narrated demo: least-privilege role management with required reasons, a credential inventory that never shows secret values, and a searchable PHI access log where viewing the log is itself audited.
demos.intro: Security and compliance reviewers want evidence, not assurances. This walkthrough covers four things. Staff roles are managed with server-enforced least privilege and a required reason for every change. A credential inventory lists what each service credential protects and who rotates it, without reading a single secret. Every PHI view is audited. And the PHI access log can be filtered and paged, and records its own use.
points: Role and facility scoping enforced on the server, with every change audited with its reason
A credential inventory that shows names and metadata only, never secret values
PHI views recorded per synthetic patient, then found in the access log seconds later
Meta-audit: viewing the log is logged, without storing the search terms typed

chapters.role-change: Changing a role, with a reason

demos.extra_disclosure: Credential names, parameter paths and service lists are blurred in this public recording. In the product, platform admins see them in full; secret values are never shown to anyone.

demos.title: EHR write-back administration (sandbox) | evrai demo
demos.h1: Designed to deliver alerts into the EHR providers already use.
demos.card_blurb: Routing, pause controls and an audited needs-attention list for alerts written back to the EHR.
demos.description: Narrated demo of Health-Connect's EHR write-back administration against a vendor sandbox: per-connection settings, routing by recommendation class, pause controls, a needs-attention list and an audited hold release. Write-back is sandbox only and not live with any customer.
demos.intro: Providers work in their EHR, so alerts should reach them there. Health-Connect's EHR write-back is designed to deliver them into the EHR as cases, routed to the right provider or queue. It is built and tested against a vendor sandbox only, and is not live with any customer. This walkthrough covers the admin side: per-connection settings and routing by recommendation class, close-reason mapping, connection and global pause, the needs-attention list, an audited hold release, and the read-only write-back panel in the review workspace.
points: One settings row per connection; production is not permitted and every change is audited
Routing by class: orders to a provider, care-team items and documentation to queues
Pause a connection, or all write-back, with held deliveries rather than failures
A needs-attention list and bundle timeline that show ids and states, never patient data

chapters.panel: Write-back panel in the review workspace

demos.extra_disclosure: EHR write-back is built and tested against a vendor sandbox only. It is not live with any customer, and production write-back is disabled.
